title: Windowed Slab Sharding with Pipeline-Boundary Awareness for Multi-GPU KV
creator: Asha Kapoor
description: Problem statement: Under mixed sequence-length workloads and pipeline/tensor parallel topologies, the KV cache becomes fragmented across GPUs and pipeline stages. This causes suboptimal packing of hot KV entries, increased inter-GPU NVLink/PCIe transfers at pipeline boundaries, uneven memory pressure, and higher tail latency during bursts. Goal: design and ship a 'windowed slab' sharding algorithm that (1) allocates KV slabs aligned to logical pipeline boundaries, (2) exposes a lightweight placement hint to the scheduler so continuous-batching groups can prefer colocated slabs, and (3) supports spill lanes and background compaction to avoid blocking hot-path inference.
design_summary: We propose dividing the KV address space into fixed-size "windows" (configurable, default 32MB) and mapping each window to a primary GPU slab that is selected based on pipeline stage ownership and recent access heat. Windows are sized to balance granularity vs. remapping cost. The placement policy considers: pipeline ownership (prefer slab on the GPU that owns the layer's KV), cross-window co-location for likely contiguous prefixes (learned from request traces), and continuous-batch affinity (batches that share prefixes are routed to compatible slabs). When memory pressure occurs, the runtime uses non-blocking background compaction and an LRU-aware spill lane to move cold windows to host/remote slab pools. This minimizes synchronous eviction in the critical path.
tradeoffs_and_risks:
- Pros: improves memory packing across pipeline stages, reduces synchronous inter-GPU transfers at boundary points, provides predictable slab sizes for allocator and profiler integration.
- Cons: extra complexity in scheduler heuristics and placement hints, potential suboptimality if access patterns change rapidly (mitigated by adaptive rebalancing), slightly increased metadata overhead for window->slab maps (~0.1% of KV size).
- Unresolved: exact default window size for models with 2k vs 16k context; we surface this as a runtime knob and will evolve after perf runs.
implementation_plan:
1) Runtime: add window metadata and slab allocator hooks; implement async compaction worker and spill lane. 2) Scheduler: extend continuous-batching router to include 'window affinity' in placement scoring. 3) Telemetry: add per-window heat and cross-stage transfer counters to Console dashboards. 4) Rollout: feature-flag behind runtime-1.20; enable on low-risk clusters for 2 weeks, then broader rollout.
Milestones: perf harness + canary (week 1), internal perf evaluation (week 2), gradual ramp (week 3).
acceptance_criteria:
- 95th percentile latency for a mixed-length benchmark (short+long tails) does not regress vs baseline; target <= +3% on average.
- Average inter-GPU bytes moved at pipeline boundaries reduced by >=20% on representative workloads.
- GPU memory fragmentation (measured as free contiguous slab ratio) improved by >=15%.
- Console shows per-window heatmaps and no increase in error rates after rollout.
- Unit and integration tests for compaction, spill, and affinity routing merged and passing in CI.
perf_results_summary: Initial cluster-level experiments (A100 x8, 4-way pipeline) on the mixed-chat benchmark: - inter-GPU boundary bandwidth dropped ~24% under steady state; - 95p latency improved 9% on long-sequence tail and remained flat for short sequences; - background compaction CPU overhead <3% and did not affect P50. Memory packing improved, yielding ~12% more usable KV capacity before spills. These are preliminary; full regression suite scheduled in cycle 2026-W11.
rollout_plan: Feature gate default off. Canary config: tina-canary (internal) with small dedicated capacity. Step 1: enable on canary clusters with detailed telemetry. Step 2: enable for dedicated-only instances with non-critical SLAs. Step 3: evaluate and enable cluster-wide with option to opt out per-customer. Provide ops playbook for rollback (feature-flag off + forced compaction).
compatibility_changes: API: no changes to public API. Internal: new runtime config 'kv.window_size' and 'kv.affinity_threshold'. Backwards compatibility: older runtime nodes will ignore hints; the placement is best-effort and falls back to baseline shard strategy.
testing_and_validation:
- Unit: window map correctness, compaction invariants, spill lane correctness.
- Integration: mixed-length continuous-batching traces replayed in perf harness.
- Chaos: simulate GPU OOM during compaction and verify graceful fallback (no request crashes).
- Load test: 72-hour soak on canary with synthetic high-variance sequence lengths.

notes: This ticket intentionally avoids changing tensor parallel KV replication model (keeps per-tensor-replica invariants) — focus is on pipeline boundary alignment and scheduler hints. If effective, follow-up ticket will explore tighter coupling with tensor-parallel KV partitioning for aggressive cross-stage co-location.
